thread:
sara: Heads up — saw a spike of ALB target deregistrations in us-west-2 around 03:12 UTC. ~60% of edge GPU pods marked Unhealthy after a scale-down/rotation.
sara: Symptoms: readiness probe timeouts, ALB health check 504/timeout, targets removed, traffic failover to warm pool. No app crash.
leo: Any node drain events at that time? Did we run spot/interruptible drain for GPU reclaim?
infra-bot: kube-events: Node gpu-usw2-azb started drain (scale-down), 02:58 UTC -> pods rescheduled.
maria: We're doing a scheduled cheap-batch scale-down to save cost across low-util windows — it pulled 12 GPU nodes simultaneously.
aj: Curious — are probes failing because of pod restarts or because healthchecks hit wrong IPs after SNAT/egress rotation?
sara: Logs show readiness probe start -> ECONNRESET for healthcheck source IP 10.2.4.12 -> then ALB sees TIMEOUT. Probes were fine before node cordon, failed after pod IP moved.
kai: That sounds like probe traffic traversing NAT and hitting ephemeral SNAT port exhaustion during bulk node churn. We've seen NAT port pressure when many pods get reallocated + EKS kube-proxy churn.
leo: Can you paste the ALB health check lines? 
infra-bot: ALB-health: target/10.2.4.12:80 health check failed (Timeout). response_time=10s status=502
maria: We recently scaled down to cut GPU cost  — wanted to confirm rollback plan if this is causing customer-facing degradation. 
aj: Short-term mitigation: 1) Pause scheduled bulk GPU scale-down 2) Increase ALB healthy threshold to avoid aggressive removal 3) Gradually drain node batches instead of all at once.
sara: Also thinking of: enable node-local SNAT (aws-node-termination-handler notes), or move healthchecks to IP target type so ALB hits instance ENI directly instead of pod IPs routed through NAT.
kai: IP target type helps but not available for our setup unless we switch ALB->NLB or enable target-type=ip with pod ENIs. Work involved.
leo: Ops play: revert today's scale-down, or roll a quick canary of 2 nodes at a time. We can't afford more 504s.
maria: Cost impact estimate: pausing scale-down keeps ~12 GPU nodes up for 6 hrs -> ~ $3,500 extra for the window vs potential SLA violations. Recommend pause.
aj: Longer-term: 1) split node pools for edge-serving vs batch to avoid co-scheduling churn 2) centralize NAT via high-capacity NAT gateway or increase ephemeral SNAT range 3) tune readinessProbe to be more tolerant during IP moves.
sara: I've applied a 3hr hold on autoscaler for gpu-edge pool. Monitoring now. If we still see healthcheck removals, proceed to revert to older node pool config.
leo: Thanks — monitor ALB dashboard and `kubectl get endpoints` for flapping. Ping here with any new failures. :thumbsup:
maria: Also opening infra ticket to evaluate NAT capacity and cost tradeoffs (NAT gateway vs increased egress IPs). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521
infra-bot: Incident note created INF-4521 by maria
sara: Update: after pausing scale-down, number of unhealthy targets dropped to normal in 8 minutes. Looks strongly correlated to concurrent node rotation. We'll follow up with a postmortem and recommended config changes.
leo: Good catch. Next steps: schedule smaller drain batches, evaluate node-local SNAT, and get cost numbers for NAT gateway resize."
